subject: physics
question_text: What is centripetal force? Write its expression and give one example.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The force that keeps a body moving on a
circular path, always directed towards the
centre of the circle, is called the
steps.why: It is not a new kind of force: in different situations tension, gravity or friction is the force that points to the centre.
common_mistakes: Treating it as an extra force that appears on its own, separate from tension or gravity.

recall.must_convey: That centripetal force keeps a body on a circular path and points towards the centre.
accept: keeps the body on a circular path

steps.memory_tip: Centripetal means centre-seeking. The name gives the direction.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words "towards the centre" are what is marked here.

steps.label: Expression and example

lines.text: F = m v² / r = m ω² r

lines: Example: when a stone tied to a string is

steps.why: Naming which real force provides it is what the second mark is for; "centripetal force" alone names nothing.
common_mistakes: Writing the expression with r in the numerator, as m v² r.

recall.must_convey: That F equals m v squared by r, equal to m omega squared r, and the tension in a whirled string is an example.

steps.memory_tip: r is below in mv²/r and above in mω²r. Substitute v = ωr to check which is which.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Formula, then example, then name the force — tension. Three short lines.

insider_note: The second mark covers the formula and the example together. Name the real force that supplies it — tension, gravity or friction.
